newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weaker yen boosts Yamaha's motorcycle profits.
newsitem.headline: Weaker yen boosts Yamaha's motorcycle profits.

text.p: Yamaha Motor Co. Ltd., the world's second-biggest motorcycle maker, said Wednesday the weaker Japanese yen helped boost its half-year profits, which almost tripled.
Yamaha said its parent current profit in the first half rose because of the weaker yen, cost-cutting and increased motorcycle sales abroad.

Yamaha's six-month current profit jumped 270 percent to 4.53 billion yen ($40.8 million). Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
"The weaker yen is a major part of the upward revisions in motorcycle exports this business year, making Japanese products more competitive on pricing," a Yamaha spokesman said.

Other top motorcycle makers, such as Honda Motor Co. Ltd., the world leader, and Suzuki Motor Corp., also said exports for the fiscal year ending March 31 would be higher than earlier predicted, but still down from the year-ago period.
The dollar is now worth about 111 yen, up from about 80 yen at the start of the previous fiscal year in April 1995.
